questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Guatemala about 108,889 square kilometres; Dominican Republic about 48,671 square kilometres; Belize about 22,966 square kilometres; El Salvador about 21,041 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Guatemala on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Guatemala on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Guatemala?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Guatemala on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Guatemala article.

questions.proof: It borders Mexico, Belize, Honduras, and El Salvador.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Guatemala?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Guatemala is the quetzal.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Guatemala?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Guatemala article.

questions.proof: To the northeast is the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Honduras and its capital and largest city is Guatemala City.
